.qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/rules/harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/SKILL.md (delivery profile, known false positives: credentials the profile expects)
evidence: Shipped data files: environment/assets/seed_data.json and solution/app/seed/seed_data.json (byte-identical, sha256 f69616e2e3d42c3ab858192126cde96cc5a39786f7f21c450b25c4ed6559be36, matching raw-evidence-index.json) plus solution/app/package.json; all parse as JSON; no CSV/TSV shipped. Scripted integrity check (python -I, scratch only) over the seed found zero problems: 17 message ids K-1..K-17 unique across 3 matters; every author is a seeded account; no author is walled from the matter they wrote in (M-12 walled=[dev], dev authors nothing there); clients author only in their own matters (gwen M-11/M-13, paul M-12); every matter client has role client; walled list holds staff only; every timer_days (7, null, 30) is in timer_options_days [null,1,7,30]; all 5 reply parents (K-14->K-1, K-15->K-14, K-4->K-3, K-12->K-6, K-9->K-8) resolve to an earlier message in the same matter; no message or version is later than clock 2026-05-12T11:00:00Z; every read_up_to user exists, every referenced matter is visible to that user (dev has no M-12 entry, paul only M-12, gwen only M-11/M-13), and every read_up_to message id exists in that matter and survives the first purge (K-3,K-4,K-6,K-8,K-9,K-12,K-16). Every K-/M- id named anywhere in tests/, instruction.md or /instructions resolves in the seed (zero missing). Seed agrees with the public brief: accounts/names/roles equal walls-and-retention.md:56-62; 'Dev Anand is walled from M-12' (walls-and-retention.md:66) equals M-12.walled; timer options equal walls-and-retention.md:74; clock equals integration.md:49. Deliberate edge fixtures are publicly explained, not inconsistencies: K-1 (11.08 days, not held) and K-10 (exactly 7.000 days) expire on the 7-day M-11 per 'a message sent exactly seven days ago on a seven-day matter is already gone' (walls-and-retention.md:74), while K-11 at +1s survives; K-14's parent K-1 therefore becomes the publicly required 'original message was deleted' placeholder (walls-and-retention.md:76), not an orphan; held K-2/K-17/K-15/K-7 and edited K-2/K-13 versions exercise hold/version rules. Synthetic: all emails use the reserved .test TLD; firm 'Kittle & Rowe', people and 'Fenwick Mills' are fictional context with no addresses, phone numbers, DOBs, IDs or financial identifiers. The personal name 'Dev Anand' coincides with a well-known public figure's name, but no real personal data is attached and the internal annotation (Internal Quality Checks row 15 F: 'dob, name, age, we can leave') permits names. No credentials in seed data (grep for password/token/api key/sk-: no hit); the shared demo password password123 lives only in the brief (walls-and-retention.md:54), which SKILL.md and the internal annotation (row 15 G) treat as expected profile. Injection: no judge-directed text (grep 'ignore previous', 'system prompt', no hit). K-16's 'Schedule 2 clause 4 rent' and K-12's '*Schedule 4*' are benign formatting fixtures for the public rule that only *bold*/code/quote/links render and other markup 'shows exactly as it was typed' (conversations.md:22); they carry no script, event handler or URL payload and the golden escapes them (server.js:506 esc(msg.body)). Adversarial: a broken app cannot gain from the seed (no pre-satisfied probe values relate to this row); a conforming alternative reading read_up_to as a message id, parent as same-matter reply and versions as earlier bodies is the only consistent reading of the data, so the seed does not penalise conforming builds. The template's placeholder seed ("CHANGE_ME") has been replaced. No runtime measurement is required for this row; the check is a static data audit fully performed here.
